newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BOURSE QUESTIONS SMALL CAPS CANDIDATE IBT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BOURSE QUESTIONS SMALL CAPS CANDIDATE IBT.

text.p: The Brussels bourse said on Wednesday it was questioning a cancer treatment firm, which is aiming to list on Belgium's new small capitalisation market, about a complaint lodged against the company in a U.S. court.

The Belgian firm, International Brachytherapy (IBt), had looked destined to become the first company to trade on the Euro.NM market in Brussels - which has yet to see its first listing - after its successful initial public offering of 250,000 shares.
But the bourse said that, in order to protect future investors, it needed to ask more questions about legal claims against IBt before deciding if and when it would be listed.
"We are studying the file and we are waiting for the answers from them to questions...relating to the claims," Eric Ronge of the Brussels bourse told Reuters.

IBt said in a statement on March 4 the U.S. company Theragenics Corp had lodged a civil complaint with a court in Georgia against IBt and its founders, claiming the latter had appropriated business secrets and confidential information belonging to Theragenics.
IBt's managers are former founders and employees of Nasdaq-listed competitor Theragenics. The statement said IBt refuted the allegations made against it.
It noted too that the claim was vague and did not refer to patent requests transfered to IBt.

IBt plans to develop, make and sell radiotherapeutic devices, called seeds, which can be implanted in a patient to treat prostate cancer in its early stages. The product will intitially target the U.S. market.
Antwerp broker Smeets, Verbaet & Co, which is bringing IBt to the market, said on Wednesday it was meeting with the Brussels stock exchange on Thursday about the matter.
Ronge, who is the Brussels Euro.NM project manager, said the exchange's management committee could refuse a company a listing if it considered this would be against market interests.
A decision would be made on IBt in the next five to 10 days.
Smeets' head of corporate finance Jean-Luc Amez said if necessary IBt could approach the equivalent French, Dutch or German Euro.NM markets for a listing. "The door is open for IBt," he said.

The Brussels Euro.NM - or New Market - is part of a wider project to form a federation of similar markets in Paris, Amsterdam and Frankfurt, rivalling the recently set up pan-European Brussels-based Easdaq market.
The Paris Nouveau Marche has been running for several months, while Frankfurt's New Market started in a burst of publicity last Monday.
Ronge said it was expected the Brussels market would see its first listing at the end of March or the beginning of April.

Second in line after IBt for listing is British clothing maker Pex Plc , followed by Belgian firm Synergia Holdings, which takes majority stakes in building material, transport and equipment makers with growth potential.
